questions.question:
In the namespace `dev`:

- create a ConfigMap `app-config` with the key `APP_MODE=production`
- create a Secret `app-secret` with the key `DB_PASS=s3cret`
- create a Pod `app` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`) that gets `APP_MODE` from the ConfigMap and `DB_PASS` from the Secret as environment variables with the same names

verification.description: ConfigMap and Secret hold the values
app takes APP_MODE and DB_PASS from them

questions.question: Create a Job `pi` in the namespace `dev` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sh -c "echo 3.14159"`) that completes `2` times with a parallelism of `2` and `backoffLimit: 4`. Wait until it has completed.

Create a CronJob `backup` in the namespace `dev` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sh -c "echo backup"`) that runs every 5 minutes (`*/5 * * * *`), with `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid`, keeping only `2` successful Jobs in its history.

In the namespace `media`, create:

- a headless Service `db` (`clusterIP: None`) selecting `app=db` on port `6379`
- a StatefulSet `db` with `2` replicas of `redis:7.2` (container port `6379`, Pod label `app=db`) that uses `serviceName: db`

Both Pods (`db-0`, `db-1`) must be running.
Create a HorizontalPodAutoscaler for the Deployment `gateway` in the namespace `payments` that keeps between `2` and `6` replicas, targeting `70%` average CPU utilization.

Update the Deployment `catalog` in the namespace `media` to the image `nginx:1.27` with a rolling update and wait until it is fully rolled out.

Then write the **number of revisions** that `kubectl rollout history` shows for it to `/tmp/exam/q6/catalog-revisions.txt` on `cka-q6`.

verification.description: catalog runs nginx:1.27 and is rolled out

questions.question:
The nodes have a `zone` label (`east` or `west`).

Create a Pod `east-pod` in the namespace `default` (image `nginx:1.27`) that uses **required node affinity** (not a `nodeSelector`) so that it can only run on nodes in the zone `east`. It must be running.

verification.description: east-pod uses required node affinity on zone=east
east-pod runs on a zone=east node

questions.question:
In the namespace `dev`, the Pod `restricted` (label `role=restricted`) must only be able to open **egress** connections to:

- Pods labeled `app=api` in the same namespace, on TCP port `80`
- DNS (UDP and TCP port `53`) in the namespace `kube-system`

Create the NetworkPolicy `restrict-egress` in `dev`. Test targets: the `api` Pods (`app=api`) must be reachable, the Pod `sink` (`app=other`) must not.

verification.description: restrict-egress allows only api:80 and DNS
restricted reaches api:80 but not sink:80

questions.question:
The StorageClass `local-dyn` exists. In the namespace `payments`, create a PersistentVolumeClaim `data-dyn` requesting `2Gi` (`ReadWriteOnce`) of that class, and a Pod `writer` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`) that mounts it at `/data`.

The claim must be Bound and the Pod running.

verification.description: data-dyn requests 2Gi RWO of local-dyn and is Bound
writer mounts data-dyn at /data and runs

questions.question:
Create a ClusterRole `node-reader` that allows `get`, `list` and `watch` on `nodes`, and a ClusterRoleBinding `node-reader-dave` that grants it to the user `dave`.

`dave` must not be able to delete nodes.

verification.description: dave can read nodes but not delete them

questions.question:
The GatewayClass `nginx-gc` exists, and in the namespace `media` the Deployment `media` is exposed by the Service `media` on port `80`. There is no gateway controller, so only the resources are graded.

Create a Gateway `main-gw` in `media` of that class with one HTTP listener named `http` on port `80`, and an HTTPRoute `media-route` in `media`, attached to `main-gw`, that sends the host `media.example.com` to the Service `media` on port `80`.

verification.description: Gateway main-gw with HTTP listener http:80
HTTPRoute media-route sends media.example.com to media:80

questions.question: Using `kubectl` with **jsonpath** output, write the InternalIP address of the node `k3d-cluster-agent-0` to `/tmp/exam/q12/node-ip.txt` on `cka-q12` (the address only).
The Secret `license` in the namespace `payments` has a key `key`. Write its **decoded** value to `/tmp/exam/q13/license.txt` on `cka-q13`.

The node `k3d-cluster-agent-1` (the `pool=legacy` node) needs maintenance. Make it unschedulable and evict all workloads from it (DaemonSet Pods may stay). Leave it cordoned.

The evicted `legacy` Pods are expected to stay `Pending` afterwards, since no other node is in the legacy pool.

verification.description: k3d-cluster-agent-1 is cordoned and runs no workload Pods

questions.question:
The Service `web` in the namespace `web` has no ready endpoints although the Pods of the Deployment `web` are running: they never become `Ready`.

Find the cause and fix the **Deployment** so that the Pods become Ready and the Service gets `2` endpoints. Keep a readiness probe.

verification.description: The readiness probe checks the nginx port

questions.question:
The Pods of the Deployment `analytics` in the namespace `analytics` are stuck in `Pending`.

Find out why from the scheduler's events and fix the Deployment: each container should request `100m` CPU and `128Mi` memory. Both replicas must be available.

In the namespace `metrics`, the Deployment `exporter` runs Pods with two named container ports: `http` (`8080`) and `metrics` (`9100`).

Create a Service `exporter` that exposes port `80` → the container port named `http`, and port `9100` → the container port named `metrics`. Name the Service ports `http` and `metrics`, and refer to the container ports **by name**.

verification.description: exporter has the two named ports targeting the container ports by name

questions.question:
In the namespace `logs`, create a Pod `log-pair` with two containers that share an `emptyDir` volume `shared`, stored **in memory** with a size limit of `64Mi`:

- `writer` (image `busybox:1.36`): `sh -c 'while true; do date >> /var/log/app/app.log; sleep 5; done'`, volume mounted at `/var/log/app`
- `reader` (image `busybox:1.36`): `sh -c 'tail -F /logs/app.log'`, the same volume mounted **read-only** at `/logs`
